summary: inventory-api is running as an enabled systemd service on node1. It remained available during a real global OOM event while the kernel killed the designated memory hog, and it recovered successfully after node restarts.
actions_performed: Created inventory-api with health and inventory endpoints on port 8080.
Configured Restart=always, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, and a 128 MiB service memory limit.
Triggered a bounded global OOM event; the kernel killed the hog while the API kept its PID and served requests.
Restored swap and removed all temporary OOM-test artifacts.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified persistence using changed boot identities.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as an OOM-protected managed service
evidence.summary: Proves the service is enabled and active, returns health and inventory data, uses Restart=always, and its live process has oom_score_adj=-1000.

evidence.requirement: The memory hog is killed by the kernel while inventory-api keeps serving
evidence.summary: Captures the healthy baseline, hog score of 1000, kernel OOM kill of hog PID 2125 after consuming about 1.6 GiB, unchanged API PID 1928 with successful health response, restored swap, and preserved inventory data.

Shows healthy baseline boot ID be2f7adb-ab9f-4c2d-99cc-ea9a9d02d1ee, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 2d893ef8-d122-4585-8882-f8fab84f5e0a, and recovered enabled service, OOM protection, API data, swap, and zero remaining hog processes or units.
